title: T1608.007 — Stage Capabilities - AI Result Poisoning
subtitle: Interactive walkthrough of Stage Capabilities - AI Result Poisoning with the technique-specific attack path and defender evidence.
aria: Animated diagram: an attacker publishes a cluster of ordinary-looking pages that all recommend one download or sign-in page and cross-link each other, an AI-powered search or chatbot retrieves the cluster and cites it in an answer, an employee clicks the recommended link from the office network, lands on an impersonation page and downloads a fake installer, and the SOC joins AI-referrer, young-domain, download, and sign-in events to respond.

nodes.label: Attacker
nodes.tip: The threat actor. Publishes and cross-links ordinary-looking pages that all push one download or sign-in page.

nodes.label: AI assistant
nodes.tip: The public AI service that retrieves web content and answers with citations. It is influenced, never hacked.

nodes.label: Poison garden
nodes.tip: Attacker-hosted pages: a help article, a review site, a fake comparison blog. Built to look independent and to be cited.

nodes.label: Employee
nodes.tip: An employee who asks the assistant a work question and clicks the recommended link from the office network.

nodes.label: SOC analyst
nodes.tip: The defender. Joins AI-referrer, young-domain, download, and sign-in events into one alert chain.

steps.title: Pick the questions
steps.caption: The attacker lists what users ask AI assistants: download invoice template, best PDF converter, company how-tos. Common questions mean many future victims, so the answer is worth poisoning.
steps.defender: Nothing is visible anywhere. Brand monitoring is the only early sensor: know which questions mention your company and your brands.

steps.title: Build the poison garden
steps.caption: The attacker publishes several ordinary-looking pages: a help article, a review site, and a fake comparison blog. All of them recommend one download or sign-in page.
steps.defender: Nothing in victim logs. The pages live on attacker infrastructure and touch no company asset - but each one needs a fresh domain and certificate.

steps.title: Cross-link the sources
steps.caption: The pages cite each other so AI retrieval sees several apparently independent confirmations. The attacker adds structured data and mirrors the content on extra domains.
steps.defender: Certificate Transparency shows more new certificates on young domains. A CT watchlist is the cheapest early warning you can build.

steps.title: The AI answers
steps.caption: An AI-powered search summary or chatbot retrieves the poisoned cluster and cites it. The generated answer recommends the attacker's link as the fix.
steps.defender: No local signal: the question and the answer stay outside your network. TI researchers start flagging clusters like this in public write-ups.

steps.title: The user clicks
steps.caption: An employee asks the assistant the same question at work and clicks the recommended link. The proxy records a referrer from the AI site into a domain that is 3 days old.
steps.defender: First strong local signal: AI-site referrer into a young domain. Alert on this join and you catch most AI poisoning before any harm.

steps.title: The lure lands
steps.caption: The user lands on an impersonation page and downloads a fake installer. Endpoint telemetry notes the file, and it arrives without a mark-of-the-web zone identifier.
steps.defender: EDR file-creation event: installer written to Downloads with no Zone.Identifier. Proxy and mail telemetry can flag the same fetch.

steps.title: Payload or phishing runs
steps.caption: The installer drops an infostealer, or the user types credentials into the fake portal. The IdP flags a risky sign-in, or EDR sees stealer behavior on the workstation.
steps.defender: Detection fires: risky sign-in from an unknown device, or EDR catches credential access. This is the moment to page, not to wait.

detection.detail: The SOC has enough evidence to open an incident.

steps.title: SOC joins the dots
steps.caption: The analyst joins AI-referrer, young domain, download, and sign-in events into one chain. The domain is blocked, the poison pages are reported to the AI provider, and a brand-monitoring rule goes live.
steps.defender: Response plus feedback loop: reporting the cluster helps the provider drop the citation for everyone. Hunt for other users who clicked the same link.
